book: Nancy Caroline · Chapter 39 · Infectious and Communicable Diseases
title: Sepsis, Key Infections and a Clean Ambulance

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already do the primary survey, give oxygen and keep patients warm. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Spot sepsis early with the SIRS criteria
  2. Give fluids exactly as the BC protocols allow
  3. Know the key diseases, your follow-up, and how to clean the truck

Textbook: Chapter 39, PDF pages 3346–3399; sepsis and SIRS: Chapter 21, PDF pages 1777–1794
slides.say: Welcome back. Last time we focused on protecting yourself. Today we focus on the patient who is sick with an infection. As EMRs, you already know the routine: scene safety, the primary survey, oxygen, keeping the patient warm, and a fast transport. As a PCP, you go deeper. You need to recognize when an infection is turning into sepsis, a life-threatening reaction of the whole body, and you have a new tool, IV fluids, with clear BC limits. So today: spotting sepsis early, giving fluids the BC way, and the key diseases you'll meet, including your follow-up after an exposure and how to clean the ambulance.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。上节课讲保护自己，今天讲因感染而生病的病人。作为 EMR，你们已经熟悉常规：现场安全、初步评估、给氧、保暖、快速转运。作为 PCP 要更深入：你要认出感染何时正在变成脓毒症——一种危及生命的全身反应；你还有了新工具，静脉补液，而 BC 对它有明确限制。所以今天讲：早期识别脓毒症、按 BC 的方式补液，以及你会遇到的重点疾病，包括暴露后的随访和怎样清洁救护车。

slides.title: Assessing a patient with an infection
slides.body:
• Scene safety and routine practices before you touch
  • Coughing, or fever with a rash? Mask the patient early
  • Common complaints: fever, nausea, rash, pleuritic chest pain, shortness of breath
  • Ask: medications, events leading up, recent travel
  • Ask: is anyone at home or in the facility sick too?

Travel history belongs in every assessment of a suspected infection.
slides.say: Assess an infected patient like any medical patient, but put your own safety first. Use routine practices before you touch anyone, and if the patient is coughing or has a fever with a rash, mask them early. Common complaints are fever, nausea, a rash, pleuritic chest pain, which means chest pain that worsens when breathing in, and shortness of breath. Ask about medications, the events leading up to today, and recent travel; the textbook makes travel history routine for any suspected infection. Ask whether family or other residents are sick too. On the BC practical, your pain history uses OPQRRRST or LOTARP, and your PCP functional enquiry includes general health and the respiratory system.
slides.sayZh: 评估感染病人和评估其他内科病人一样，但先顾好自己的安全：接触任何人之前执行常规防护；病人咳嗽或发热伴皮疹，就尽早给他戴口罩。常见主诉有发热、恶心、皮疹、胸膜炎性胸痛（吸气时加重的胸痛）和气促。问用药、今天发病前的经过和近期旅行；教材把旅行史列为凡疑似感染都要问的常规。还要问家人或其他院友是否也病了。BC 实操考试里，疼痛病史用 OPQRRRST 或 LOTARP；你作为 PCP 的系统问诊包括一般健康和呼吸系统。

slides.title: SIRS: the body's alarm
slides.body:
SIRS = two or more of:

  • Temperature > 38°C or < 36°C
  • Heart rate > 90
  • Respiratory rate > 20 (or PCO₂ < 32 mm Hg)
  • White cells > 12 or < 4 × 10⁹/L (lab only)

SIRS + infection = sepsis
slides.say: The textbook's tool for spotting sepsis early is SIRS, which stands for systemic inflammatory response syndrome. It means the whole body is reacting to a serious insult. A patient has SIRS with two or more of these: a temperature above thirty-eight or below thirty-six degrees, a heart rate above ninety, a breathing rate above twenty, or an abnormal white cell count. The white count needs a lab, but you can check the other three on scene. SIRS alone isn't a diagnosis, because trauma, burns, and pancreatitis cause it too. But SIRS plus an infection equals sepsis. So a feverish, fast-breathing patient with a cough should raise your concern right away.
slides.sayZh: 教材里早期识别脓毒症的工具是 SIRS，即全身炎症反应综合征，意思是全身都在对严重打击作出反应。满足下面两条或以上就是 SIRS：体温高于三十八度或低于三十六度；心率超过九十；呼吸超过二十次；或白细胞计数异常。白细胞要靠化验，但另外三项你在现场就能查。单有 SIRS 不是诊断，因为创伤、烧伤、胰腺炎也会引起。但 SIRS 加上感染就等于脓毒症。所以一个发热、呼吸快、还咳嗽的病人，应该马上引起你的警惕。

slides.title: Septic shock: why the pressure falls
slides.body:
Sepsis + systolic < 90 (or a drop > 40 from baseline) = septic shock

  • Capillaries leak: fluid leaves the vessels
  • Vessels dilate: a bigger container
  • Leaked fluid can collect in the lungs
  • Skin may be warm and flushed, not pale
  • Higher risk: older adults, burns, diabetes, cancer
slides.say: When sepsis drops the blood pressure, it becomes septic shock: a systolic under ninety, or a fall of more than forty from the patient's normal. Three problems happen at once. The capillaries leak, so fluid escapes from the blood vessels. The vessels dilate, so the container gets bigger. And the leaked fluid can collect in the lungs and make breathing harder. Unlike most shock, the skin may be warm and flushed instead of pale, so don't let pink skin fool you. Watch for confusion, fast breathing, and low urine output. If it continues, organs fail one after another; at that stage the book gives a death rate of sixty to ninety percent.
slides.sayZh: 脓毒症让血压下降时就成了感染性休克：收缩压低于九十，或比病人平时下降超过四十。三个问题同时发生：毛细血管渗漏，液体跑出血管；血管扩张，容器变大；渗出的液体还可能积在肺里，让呼吸更困难。和大多数休克不同，病人皮肤可能温暖潮红而不是苍白，别被粉红的皮肤骗了。留意意识混乱、呼吸急促和尿量减少。如果继续发展，器官会一个接一个衰竭；书里说到那个阶段死亡率是百分之六十到九十。

slides.q: A care-home resident is newly confused and coughing. Temp 38.6°C, pulse 112, respirations 26, BP 118/70. What is your impression?
options: Probably a cold, because the blood pressure is normal
Possible sepsis: SIRS criteria plus a likely infection
Septic shock, because the pulse is over 90
You can't judge SIRS without a white cell count
slides.say: Let's check your thinking. A care-home resident is newly confused and coughing. Temperature thirty-eight point six, pulse one hundred twelve, respirations twenty-six, blood pressure one eighteen over seventy. What is your impression? A, probably a cold, because the blood pressure is normal. B, possible sepsis: SIRS criteria plus a likely infection. C, septic shock, because the pulse is over ninety. D, you can't judge SIRS without a white cell count. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 检验一下思路。一位护理院住户新出现意识混乱并咳嗽，体温三十八点六度，脉搏一百一十二，呼吸二十六，血压一百一十八比七十。你的初步判断是什么？A，大概是感冒，因为血压正常；B，可能是脓毒症：符合 SIRS 标准并有可能的感染；C，感染性休克，因为脉搏超过九十；D，没有白细胞计数就无法判断 SIRS。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. She meets three SIRS criteria, temperature, heart rate, and breathing rate, and the cough suggests a source of infection, so think sepsis. Her new confusion is a warning sign too. A is wrong because a normal blood pressure doesn't rule out sepsis. C is wrong because a fast pulse doesn't define shock; septic shock needs a systolic under ninety or a drop of more than forty from her usual. D is wrong because two criteria are enough, and you can check three on scene.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。她符合三条 SIRS 标准——体温、心率、呼吸频率——咳嗽又提示有感染源，所以要想到脓毒症；新出现的意识混乱也是警讯。A 错，血压正常不能排除脓毒症。C 错，脉搏快不等于休克；感染性休克需要收缩压低于九十，或比她平时下降超过四十。D 错，满足两条就够了，而其中三条你在现场就能查。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: fluids the BC way
slides.body:
BC Hypovolemia protocol: loss of significant blood or body fluid + systolic < 90 + other signs of shock (may start earlier if shock is expected).

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Lay the patient supine to support BP
  • Keep warm, prevent heat loss
  • Oxygen to SpO₂ ≥ 94%

PCP adds (en route or if delayed)

  • Vascular access (IV)
  • Fluid bolus 20 mL/kg, max 2 L
  • Reassess every 500 mL
  • TXA only for shock from blood loss
slides.say: Here's where your new scope comes in. In BC, the fluid rules come from the Hypovolemia protocol, which doesn't name sepsis. You use it when there's evidence of a significant loss of blood or body fluid, like vomiting or diarrhea, a systolic under ninety, and other signs of shock. The left column is what every licence level does: supine, warm, and oxygen to a saturation of ninety-four or higher. The right column is yours. En route, or if there's a delay, start an IV and give twenty millilitres per kilogram, up to two litres, reassessing every five hundred.
slides.sayZh: 这里用到你的新权限。在 BC，补液规则来自低血容量流程，而这个流程没有点名脓毒症。适用条件是：有明显失血或体液丢失的证据，比如呕吐或腹泻；收缩压低于九十；并有其他休克征象。左栏是各级别都做的：平卧、保暖、给氧使血氧达到九十四或以上。右栏是你的：在转运途中或有延误时，开静脉，每公斤二十毫升、最多两升，每五百毫升复评一次。

slides.title: Vomiting and diarrhea: the PCP protocol
slides.body:
Gastroenteritis: nausea, vomiting, fever, cramps, diarrhea. Dehydration hits children, older adults and the chronically ill.

  • BC Nausea–Vomiting protocol: PCP adds IV access
  • Dimenhydrinate or ondansetron
  • Hypotension from volume loss: 20 mL/kg, max 2 L, every 500 mL
  • Target systolic 90 mm Hg
  • Stable: anti-emetic on scene; unstable: en route

Diarrhea: gloves, and soap and water if C. difficile is possible.
slides.say: Gastroenteritis, often called stomach flu, causes nausea, vomiting, fever, cramps, and diarrhea. Healthy adults usually cope, but children, older adults, and people with chronic illness can become badly dehydrated. BC's Nausea and Vomiting protocol has a PCP part that's new for you. You may start an IV and give an anti-emetic, a drug against nausea: dimenhydrinate or ondansetron. If the patient is hypotensive from volume loss, give twenty millilitres per kilogram, up to two litres, reassessing every five hundred, with a target systolic of ninety. Stable patients can get the anti-emetic on scene; unstable patients are treated en route. For diarrhea, wear gloves, and use soap and water if C. difficile is possible.
slides.sayZh: 胃肠炎俗称肠胃型感冒，会引起恶心、呕吐、发热、腹部绞痛和腹泻。健康成人通常扛得住，但儿童、老人和慢性病患者可能严重脱水。BC 恶心呕吐流程里有一部分 PCP 内容，对你是新的：你可以开静脉，可以给止吐药——茶苯海明或昂丹司琼。如果病人因体液丢失而低血压，按每公斤二十毫升、最多两升补液，每五百毫升复评，目标收缩压九十。稳定的病人可以在现场给止吐药，不稳定的在转运途中处理。遇到腹泻要戴手套，可能是艰难梭菌时要用肥皂和流水洗手。

slides.title: Airborne or droplet: the key diseases
slides.body:
DiseaseRouteKey point for you
TBAirborneCough > 3 weeks + night sweats, weight loss: N95
Measles, chickenpoxAirborneReal protection is immunity: know your status
Meningococcal meningitisDropletSuction or intubation spray, or ≥ 8 h close contact
InfluenzaDropletYearly vaccine; antiviral within 48 h if unvaccinated
slides.say: Let's sort the key respiratory diseases by route. TB is airborne. Suspect it with a cough lasting more than three weeks plus night sweats, fever, or weight loss, and wear an N95. If you were exposed without protection, report it; you'll be tested, then retested in eight to ten weeks. Measles and chickenpox are also airborne, and your best protection is being immune, so know your vaccine status. Meningitis is different. The bacterial form spreads by droplets, not through the air, and viral meningitis doesn't spread at all. Your risk comes from suctioning, intubation spray, mouth-to-mouth, or eight hours or more of close contact. Influenza is droplet too: get your yearly flu shot.
slides.sayZh: 按传播途径把重点呼吸道病分一分。结核是空气传播：咳嗽超过三周，加盗汗、发热或体重下降就要怀疑，戴 N95。如果无防护暴露，要报告；你会做检测，八到十周后复查。麻疹和水痘也是空气传播，最好的防护是有免疫力，所以要清楚自己的疫苗状况。脑膜炎不同：细菌性脑膜炎经飞沫传播，不经空气；病毒性脑膜炎根本不传染。你的风险来自吸引、插管时的喷溅、口对口，或八小时以上的密切接触。流感也是飞沫传播：每年打流感疫苗。

slides.title: Hepatitis B, C and HIV after a stick
slides.body:
VirusProtectionAfter an exposure
Hepatitis BVaccine: start, 4 weeks, 6 months; titre 1–2 months laterPositive titre on file: no treatment. Unvaccinated + source positive: immune globulin + vaccine
Hepatitis CNo vaccine, no prophylaxisRetest at 4–6 weeks; treatment often cures it
HIVGloves, sharps safetyRapid source test (< 1 h); if positive, possibly 4 weeks of antiretrovirals
slides.say: Now the three bloodborne viruses that matter most after a needlestick. Hepatitis B is the one a vaccine prevents: a first dose, a second at four weeks, and a third at six months, then a blood test called a titre one to two months later to prove you're immune. With a positive titre on file, you need no treatment after an exposure. Hepatitis C has no vaccine and no preventive treatment, so you're retested at four to six weeks, and modern drugs can often cure it. For HIV, the source gets a rapid test with results in under an hour; if it's positive, you may take antiretroviral drugs for four weeks.
slides.sayZh: 再看针刺后最要紧的三种血源性病毒。乙肝可以靠疫苗预防：打第一针，四周后第二针，六个月时第三针，完成后一到两个月抽血查抗体滴度，证明你已免疫。档案里有阳性滴度，暴露后就不需要处理。丙肝没有疫苗，也没有暴露后预防，所以在四到六周时复查，现代药物常常能治愈。HIV：源患者做快速检测，一小时内出结果；如果阳性，你可能要服用四周抗逆转录病毒药。

slides.q: You're a PCP. A 70 kg man has vomited all day. BP 84/50, pulse 124, dry mouth, no bleeding. Transport is 20 minutes. What is the best plan?
options: Oxygen, supine, warm, transport; IV en route, 20 mL/kg up to 1,400 mL, reassess every 500 mL
Give TXA 2 g IV, because he is in shock
Run 2 L in as fast as possible, then reassess
No IV, because fluids are only for patients who are bleeding
slides.say: Here's a PCP decision. A seventy-kilogram man has vomited all day. His blood pressure is eighty-four over fifty, pulse one hundred twenty-four, his mouth is dry, and there's no bleeding. Transport is twenty minutes. What's the best plan? A, oxygen, supine, keep warm, and transport; start the IV en route and give twenty millilitres per kilogram, up to one thousand four hundred millilitres, reassessing every five hundred. B, give TXA two grams IV, because he is in shock. C, run two litres in as fast as possible, then reassess. D, no IV, because fluids are only for patients who are bleeding. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一名七十公斤男子呕吐了一整天，血压八十四比五十，脉搏一百二十四，口干，没有出血，转运二十分钟。最佳方案是？A，给氧、平卧、保暖、出发，途中开静脉，按每公斤二十毫升给、最多一千四百毫升，每五百毫升复评；B，因为他休克，静脉给 TXA 两克；C，尽快输进两升再复评；D，不开静脉，因为补液只给出血的病人。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is A. He's hypotensive from fluid loss, so the BC protocols apply: basic care, transport, then an IV en route with twenty millilitres per kilogram, which is one thousand four hundred millilitres for seventy kilograms, reassessing every five hundred, aiming for a systolic of ninety. B is wrong because TXA is only for shock from blood loss. C is wrong because you reassess every five hundred millilitres, not after two litres. D is wrong because BC counts the loss of body fluids, not just blood.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 A。他因体液丢失而低血压，适用 BC 流程：先做基础处理、出发，途中开静脉，每公斤二十毫升，七十公斤就是一千四百毫升，每五百毫升复评，目标收缩压九十。B 错，TXA 只用于失血引起的休克。C 错，每五百毫升就要复评，不是输完两升再看。D 错，BC 认可体液丢失，不只是失血。

slides.title: Resistant germs and new diseases
slides.body:
• MRSA: spread mainly by unwashed hands; drainage on intact skin = no exposure
  • VRE: lives on surfaces a long time; clean every contact area
  • Neither has post-exposure treatment: report and document
  • Ebola-type fevers: gloves, mask, eyewear, face shield, impermeable gown
  • Fever after recent travel: tell the receiving hospital early
slides.say: Some germs no longer respond to common antibiotics. MRSA, a resistant staph bacterium, spreads mostly on unwashed hands, and many health care workers carry it in their noses. If its drainage touches your intact skin, that's not an exposure. VRE, another resistant bacterium, survives on surfaces for a long time, so clean every area the patient touched. Neither has a post-exposure treatment, so report and document. Every few years a new disease appears, like SARS, MERS, or Ebola. For Ebola and similar bleeding fevers, wear gloves, a mask, eye protection, a face shield, and an impermeable gown, meaning fluids can't soak through. That's why travel history matters: pass it to the hospital early.
slides.sayZh: 有些病菌对常用抗生素已经无效。MRSA 是一种耐药的金黄色葡萄球菌，主要靠没洗的手传播，很多医护人员鼻腔里就带着它。它的引流液碰到你完整的皮肤，不算暴露。VRE 是另一种耐药菌，能在物体表面存活很久，所以病人碰过的每个地方都要清洁。这两种都没有暴露后治疗，所以要报告并记录。每隔几年就会出现新病，比如 SARS、MERS、埃博拉。对埃博拉这类出血热，要戴手套、口罩、护目镜、面罩，穿防渗隔离衣，也就是液体渗不透的那种。这就是旅行史重要的原因：要尽早告诉医院。

slides.title: Cleaning the ambulance
slides.body:
Book's levelExamplesHow
CriticalLaryngoscope blades, airway tubesSingle use, or high-level disinfection
SemicriticalStethoscope, BP cuff, splintsA product that kills hepatitis B, e.g. bleach 1:100
NoncriticalFloors, seats, countersHospital-grade cleaner or bleach

Clean first, then disinfect. TB and measles need only routine cleaning. Follow your service's policy.
slides.say: Cleaning protects your next patient from an infection caught in the ambulance. The textbook sorts equipment into three levels. Critical items touch mucous membranes, like laryngoscope blades and airway tubes; they're single-use or get high-level disinfection. Semicritical items touch intact skin, like stethoscopes, cuffs, and splints; use a product labelled to kill hepatitis B, such as bleach diluted one to one hundred. Noncritical surfaces, like floors and seats, need a hospital-grade cleaner. Always clean before you disinfect, because disinfectant can't work through dirt. After TB or measles, routine cleaning is enough. Other systems label these levels differently, so follow your service's policy. And don't come to work with a sore throat or a cold.
slides.sayZh: 清洁是为了保护下一位病人，不让他在救护车里染上感染。教材把器械分三级。关键器械接触黏膜，比如喉镜片和气道导管，要一次性使用或做高水平消毒。半关键器械接触完整皮肤，比如听诊器、袖带、夹板，要用标明能杀灭乙肝病毒的产品，比如一比一百稀释的漂白水。非关键表面，比如地板和座椅，用医院级清洁剂。一定先清洁再消毒，因为消毒剂穿不透污垢。运送结核或麻疹病人后，常规清洁就够了。其他体系对这几级的叫法不同，以你所在机构的规定为准。还有，喉咙痛或感冒时别来上班。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Warm, pink skin and a normal BP don't rule out sepsis
  • Shock fluids: don't hold the scene; IV en route or if delayed
  • Listen to the lungs before and after each 500 mL
  • TXA is for blood loss, not infection or vomiting
  • Ondansetron: not with congenital long QT; ask first
  • CPAP or nebulizer on a febrile, coughing patient: N95 + eyewear
slides.say: Now the new things to watch for. First, sepsis can hide: warm, pink skin and a normal blood pressure don't rule it out. Second, don't hold the scene to start fluids for shock; the BC hypovolemia protocol puts the IV en route, or on scene only if there's a delay. Third, septic capillaries leak, so listen to the lungs before you start fluids and after every five hundred millilitres. Fourth, TXA is only for shock from blood loss. Fifth, before ondansetron, ask about congenital long QT syndrome; BC advises asking Indigenous patients about family history, and using dimenhydrinate if it's present. Sixth, CPAP or a nebulizer on a feverish, coughing patient means an N95 and eye protection.
slides.sayZh: 现在是需要注意的新事项。第一，脓毒症会伪装：皮肤温暖粉红、血压正常都不能排除它。第二，不要为了给休克病人补液而滞留现场；BC 低血容量流程把开静脉放在转运途中，只有延误时才在现场开。第三，脓毒症的毛细血管会渗漏，所以开始补液前和每五百毫升之后都要听肺。第四，TXA 只用于失血引起的休克。第五，给昂丹司琼前要问有没有先天性长 QT 综合征；BC 建议问原住民病人的家族史，有的话改用茶苯海明。第六，对发热咳嗽的病人用 CPAP 或雾化，就要戴 N95 和护目镜。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. SIRS (2+ of temp, pulse > 90, breathing > 20, WBC) + infection = sepsis
  2. BC fluids: en route, 20 mL/kg, max 2 L, reassess every 500 mL
  3. Airborne three need an N95; hepatitis C has no vaccine and no prophylaxis

Next: Chapter 40, Behavioural Emergencies
slides.say: Let's wrap up with three things to remember. One: two or more SIRS criteria plus an infection means sepsis. Check temperature, pulse, and breathing rate, and don't be reassured by a normal blood pressure. Two: BC fluids for volume loss and shock: start the IV en route, give twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres, and reassess every five hundred. Three: TB, measles, and chickenpox are the airborne three that need an N95, and hepatitis C has no vaccine and no preventive treatment, so sharps safety is your real protection. Next chapter: behavioural emergencies. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，满足两条或以上 SIRS 标准再加感染，就是脓毒症；要查体温、脉搏和呼吸频率，别因为血压正常就放心。二，BC 对体液丢失和休克的补液：途中开静脉，每公斤二十毫升、最多两升，每五百毫升复评。三，结核、麻疹、水痘是要戴 N95 的空气传播三病；丙肝没有疫苗也没有暴露后预防，锐器安全才是你真正的保护。下一章讲行为急症。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
